text.characters:
Welcome to our comprehensive resource page dedicated to connecting carers with dementia care services.
Living with dementia or caring for someone who does, can bring a range of physical, emotional, and financial challenges. We have curated a list of essential services to assist you. By inputting your location on the profile page, you will be able to see dementia services in your local area. You can also search for specific service types (e.g. hospital) in the search bar.
Dementia caregiving encompasses multiple facets, and there are support services available for each aspect. These include; government-funded aged care services (my aged care) and the NDIS for those diagnosed with dementia before the age of 65. Carer support is available from Carer Gateway, Carers Australia and Carer Support Groups, you can also seek support from carers under the Peer-Support tab here on e-DiVA. Support for keeping your loved one at home is available at Independent Living Centres and support for changed behaviours can be found with through Dementia Support Australia, including their Dementia Behaviour Management Advisory Services. Respite care can be arranged through the Commonwealth Respite and Carelink Centres.
Try searching for any of these services to see what is available near you.
For more information and support services please refer to module 6 in the iSupport course.
